candidates.name: Gastrointestinal graft-versus-host disease
support_spans: 3 months of hematochezia
mixed blood
eroded surface mucosa with reactive hyperplastic glands
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and histologic examination results are consistent with gastrointestinal involvement.

candidates.name: Inflammatory bowel disease
support_spans: two to three loose bowel movements per day
abdomen was soft and nontender
contradict_spans: Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms could be indicative of inflammatory bowel disease, but negative stool studies reduce the likelihood.

candidates.name: Whipple disease
support_spans: marked expansion of the lamina propria by a dense mixed inflammatory infiltrate
basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions
contradict_spans: Additional fungal and acid-fast stains were negative for organisms
candidates.why: The histologic findings could be consistent with Whipple disease, but negative special stains reduce the likelihood.

candidates.name: Malakoplakia
support_spans: basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains
candidates.why: The presence of Michaelis-Gutmann bodies is consistent with malakoplakia.

candidates.name: Familial adenomatous polyposis
support_spans: multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon
contradict_spans: Histologic examination of the polyps revealed eroded surface mucosa with reactive hyperplastic glands
candidates.why: The presence of multiple polyps could be indicative of familial adenomatous polyposis, but the histologic findings do not support this diagnosis.
